description:
FILED s465ba (Opus, round 23) while shipping #1028.  PRE-EXISTING; #1028 fixed
the ref/glob/qr/object/undef half and deliberately left this one.

PERL'S RULE (pp_bit_and): the op is NUMERIC iff `SvNIOKp(left) ||
SvNIOKp(right)` -- iff an SV carries a number.  A string LITERAL is PV-only,
so it does NOT, and `"12" & "10"` is the bit-string op:

    perl -e 'printf "%vd\n", ("12" & "10")'      # 49.48  = "10"
    perl -e 'my $x = "12"; my $j = $x + 0;
             printf "%vd\n", ($x & "10")'        # 56     = "8"  (NOW numeric)

The second line is the flag at work: reading a PV as a number sets SvNIOKp,
and the SAME text then takes the other path.  PCL has no such flag, so
`p-string-bitwise-operand-p` asks `looks-like-number` instead -- a purely
TEXTUAL question, which answers "numeric" for the first line too.

MEASURED DIVERGENCES TODAY (scratch/p1-perl-rule.pl rows 2/3/6,
p2-perl-more.pl row 26, p3-perl-complement.pl "num str"), all on both
emission paths:

    "12" & "10"     perl "10" (3130)   PCL "8"  (38)
    "12" | "10"     perl "12" (3132)   PCL "14" (3134)
    ~"22"           perl "\xcd\xcd"    PCL 18446744073709551593

SIBLING DIVERGENCE FROM THE SAME MISSING FLAG (probed, p2 row 36): `$!` is a
DUALVAR -- IOK and POK -- so `$! | "x"` is NUMERIC in perl and STRING in PCL.
PCL's box HAS the discriminator for this one (`p-box-nv-ok`, set by `box-nv`
when it numifies and by `p-dualvar` at construction), so a `(and (p-box-p v)
(p-box-nv-ok v))` arm in `%p-bitwise-operand-kind` would answer it exactly.
That arm was NOT taken in #1028 because it makes the mode HISTORY-DEPENDENT
and nothing measured needed it; take it WITH the pragma work, and measure the
sweep for false positives (any runtime path that numifies a box for its own
reasons would then flip the mode).

THE BLOCKER, and it is a real feature: `use feature 'bitwise'` (default from
`use v5.28`) makes `& | ^ ~` ALWAYS numeric and `&. |. ^. ~.` always string.
PCL implements the DOTTED spellings but does not track the pragma at all, so
today `"22" & "66"` inside such a block is answered numerically BY ACCIDENT of
`looks-like-number` -- and perl-tests/bop.t lines 365-410 assert exactly that
(11 rows across its `use feature "bitwise"` and `use v5.27` blocks, all
passing today).  Remove the heuristic without the pragma and those 11 rows
break.

FIX SHAPE (sized, not attempted): the pragma is LEXICALLY scoped to a BLOCK,
so `_signatures_enabled_at`'s line/column model is NOT enough -- bop.t closes
its `{ use feature "bitwise"; ... }` and the ref tests after it need the
DEFAULT semantics.  The right sibling is `use integer`, which is already
block-scoped through `Pl::Environment::set_pragma` / `has_pragma` on the scope
frame (Pl/Parser.pm:8941).  So: set a `feature_bitwise` pragma the same way
(also for `use v5.28`+ and the `:5.NN` bundles), and in Pl/ExprToCL.pm's
%BINARY_OPS map emit numeric-only variants under it.  New runtime entry points
(`p-num-bit-and` etc., or a flag argument) rather than a second decision
inside `%p-bitwise-operand-kind` -- the pragma is a COMPILE-time fact.

KNOWN CONSEQUENCE OF #1028 THAT THIS CLOSES: under `use feature 'bitwise'`,
`"\x{100}" | "\xFF"` now DIES in PCL (the over-0xFF fatal, correct for the
string op) where perl runs the numeric op.  Before #1028 it was silently
wrong.  Probed: scratch/p3-perl-complement.pl's `feat` rows.
subject: SILENT WRONG (the remaining half of #1028): a numeric-LOOKING string still takes the NUMERIC bitwise op -- `"12" & "10"` is "10" in perl and "8" in PCL -- because `looks-like-number` is PCL's stand-in for perl's per-SV "has been used as a number" flag.  Closing it REQUIRES `use feature 'bitwise'` first: under that pragma `&` is ALWAYS numeric and perl-tests/bop.t asserts exactly that for `"22" & "66"`, so removing the heuristic without the pragma breaks 11 rows that pass today.
